events.strDescriptionEN:
The London ePrix is an annual race of the single-seater, electrically powered Formula E championship, held in London, United Kingdom. It was first raced in the 2014–15 season until the 2015–16 season. The event was originally meant to return for the 2019–20 season at a new location around (and through) ExCeL London before being cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The event at the new location was eventually held in the following season.

Taylor Barnard achieved his maiden Formula E victory in a chaotic and dramatic season-ending London E-Prix (Race 2) at ExCeL London. Driving for DS Penske, the 22-year-old became the youngest-ever race winner in Formula E history.
Meanwhile, Pascal Wehrlein was crowned the 2025–26 Formula E World Champion, securing his second career title despite a late-race collision with Jake Dennis that left both drivers completely outside of the point-scoring positions.
